question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $g(x)=3x+4$ and $f(g(x))=g(x{)}^{5}.$ 

Differentiating, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(g(x)) & =({g}^{5}{)}^{′}=5{g}^{4}, \\ {g}^{′}(x) & =(3x+4{)}^{′}=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the chain rule, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={f}^{′}(g(x))\cdot {g}^{′}(x) \\  & =5{g}^{4}\cdot 3 \\  & =15(3x+4{)}^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $g(x)=3 x^{5} - x^{2}$ and $f(g(x))=g^{3}.$ 

Differentiating, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(g(x)) & =(g^{3})^{′}=3 g^{2}, \\ {g}^{′}(x) & =(3 x^{5} - x^{2})^{′}=15 x^{4} - 2 x.\end{aligned}

Then, using the chain rule, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={f}^{′}(g(x))\cdot {g}^{′}(x) \\  & =(3 g^{2})\cdot (15 x^{4} - 2 x) \\  & =\left(45 x^{4} - 6 x\right) \left(3 x^{5} - x^{2}\right)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $g(x)=2 x^{2} + x$ and $f(g(x))=\frac{2}{\sqrt{g}}.$ 

Differentiating, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(g(x)) & =(\frac{2}{\sqrt{g}})^{′}=- \frac{1}{g^{\frac{3}{2}}}, \\ {g}^{′}(x) & =(2 x^{2} + x)^{′}=4 x + 1.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the chain rule, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={f}^{′}(g(x))\cdot {g}^{′}(x) \\  & =(- \frac{1}{g^{\frac{3}{2}}})\cdot (4 x + 1) \\  & =\frac{2 \left(- 2 x - \frac{1}{2}\right)}{\left(2 x^{2} + x\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$
